lines.en: What makes language such a powerful tool is that it can carry an idea from one mind to another.
It is estimated that half of the world's seven thousand languages may disappear within a century.
Not until a language loses its last speaker does it truly die.
However good a translation may be, something of the original always stays behind.
Were everyone in the world to speak one language, we would understand each other better but think less richly.
The expression is said to have traveled from old Cairo markets into everyday speech.
It is not the words themselves, but the tone and the silence between them, that carry the real meaning.
Little attention is paid to how many new words technology adds to our speech every year.
What children teach us about language is that rules are learned by listening, not by studying.
Rarely does anyone think about the thousands of voices that shaped a single word over the centuries.
What every translator knows is that some feelings exist only in the language that named them.
It is through stories, not dictionaries, that a language truly survives.
Not until he moved abroad did he realize how much of his personality lived in his mother tongue.
Were a language to be lost every two weeks, as experts warn, the world would grow poorer in ways we cannot measure.
It is the words we choose, more than the words we know, that show who we are.
